tagline: Over the mountain the interstate goes under.
intro: Between Bland and Wytheville, Interstate 77 goes through Big Walker Mountain in a tunnel. The byway goes over it instead, about 16 miles of Route 717 and US 52 in the Jefferson National Forest, with overlooks onto the ridge-and-valley country and, from the top, a view that reaches Mount Rogers, the highest peak in Virginia.
The mountain is named for Thomas Walker, who came through in 1749. In July 1863 Molly Tynes crossed it by this same route to warn Wytheville that Union cavalry were coming.

moments.title: Bland
moments.text: The county seat at the Bland end of the byway began as Bland Court House and counted 312 people at the 2020 census.

moments.title: Big Walker Lookout
moments.text: Just off US 52 a 100-foot tower built in 1947 stands at 3,405 feet, and the view from its top takes in mountain peaks in five states.

moments.title: Wytheville
moments.text: The town at the foot of the byway was called Evansham until a fire in 1839, and Molly Tynes's warning reached it in time for Toland's raid in 1863.
